contexts.text: Like masked mountebanks and mimics on the stage.
They play with Divine things like mountebanks.
So comedians and mimics know how to represent kings, etc... when yet they are nothing but actors.
Like a mountebank, who, with his body upside down, walks upon the palms of his hands. TCR 381:end.
Then, concerning the spiritual things of the Church... he thinks no otherwise than as a mountebank.
A mountebank wishes only to mountebank (or talk silly stuff).
Like a mountebank upon a stage, who can personate two characters, by running from one side to the other...
Concerning sorceries, magical arts, soothsayings, and the like.
So sciences and philosophy, by which a man supposes that he can rule spiritual and celestial things, are like soothsayings and sorceries...
When they come... among such as are called sorcerers, soothsayers, etc.
(I compared) their speech to the speech of mountebanks on this Earth, who speak with their fingers, and... with inverted words...

Their magical arts are most absurd. They are like mountebanks: they move their loins and feet, bend them, then their bodies, and their arms... They are most absurd mountebanks: they prostrate themselves, circumrotate themselves, make themselves invisible...
Their priests and wise ones were called magi and soothsayers.
The priests and diviners of the Philistines () persuaded them to make images of the haemorrhoids and mice; for their priests and diviners then knew what all these things represented...
5. Behold, it was a theatre of stage players, where they mountebanked in masks, and became fools.
To represent the orgies of Bacchus and the mountebankisms of comedians.
